access_continuity_justification: The organization has three owners, fametrano, giacomocaironi and pmazzocchi, each an administrator of this repository and a reviewer of its pypi and testpypi environments. If one becomes unavailable, the other two can still close issues, merge changes and release. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The package is a library of functions with no user interface: no terminal prompt, no GUI and no web front end, and nothing under src/ calls input or print. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/tree/main/src/coin_addresses
assurance_case_justification: This repository has no assurance case: no document gives its threat model, its trust boundaries, the secure design principles it applies or how each common weakness is countered. SECURITY.md says what counts as a vulnerability here and what is known and not defended, which is not an assurance case. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/SECURITY.md
automated_integration_testing_justificat: test.yml runs the suite on every push to main, each pull request's merge included: its push trigger carries no path filter, and its changes job finds code changed for every event but a pull request. A run that a newer push to main supersedes is cancelled, and the newer run tests the tree that holds both. On a pull request the suite runs unless the pull request is a draft or changes only prose, as the prose-pattern of its changes job defines it: the root Markdown files the pattern names, README.md not among them, .github's own Markdown and the secrets baseline. A draft cannot be merged, and a prose-only change has no code to test. Its aggregate job `test: every job passed`, which accepts a skipped job, is a required check. The os-ubuntu, os-macos and os-windows workflows run the suite on every supported interpreter weekly and in every release run, as they did for v2026.11.14 (https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/actions/runs/43524763358). https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml
build_common_tools_justification: The build uses uv with the uv_build backend, the standard tools of a Python package. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses?tab=contributing-ov-file
build_floss_tools_justification: uv, uv_build, and every tool CONTRIBUTING.md names are FLOSS. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses?tab=contributing-ov-file
build_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md gives the build: uv is the only prerequisite, uv sync builds the environment from uv.lock and uv build produces the sdist and wheel. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses?tab=contributing-ov-file
build_non_recursive_justification: This tree builds no native binaries, so there is no recursive-build question to answer. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/pyproject.toml
build_preserve_debug_justification: No native build or installation step exists to strip or preserve debugging information. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/pyproject.toml
build_repeatable_justification: Rebuilt from the tag v2026.11.14 with the uv named in the wheel, 0.13.8, the sdist and the wheel are byte-identical to the released files (SHA-256 compared on 2026-11-14). sdist-rebuild.yml is scheduled weekly to rebuild the latest release's sdist from its tag, and passes only if it matches the release's attested digest. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/.github/workflows/sdist-rebuild.yml
build_reproducible_justification: The sdist is built with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH from the commit and normalized by .github/scripts/normalize_sdist.py. A rebuild of v2026.11.14 by RELEASING.md's Rebuild a release from its tag gave the same SHA-256 as the released sdist, wheel and SBOM on 2026-11-14, and the release's attestation verified each rebuilt file. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/RELEASING.md#rebuild-a-release-from-its-tag
build_standard_variables_justification: This tree builds no native binaries -- it is pure Python on the uv_build backend -- so there is no compiler or linker invocation for CC/CFLAGS/LDFLAGS to reach. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/pyproject.toml
bus_factor_justification: fametrano wrote almost all of the code and is the only person who knows it in depth. The repository opened on 2026-11-12. Of the 22 commits the tag v2026.11.14 holds, 18 are fametrano's, 3 are Dependabot's and 1 is an outside contributor's (IG-ABHINAV, pull request 7, a comment in deps-latest.yml). Counted with: git rev-list --count v2026.11.14, and git log v2026.11.14 --format=%an | sort | uniq -c. pmazzocchi and giacomocaironi, the other organization owners, have made no commit here; the owners administer every repository. Knowledge of the code rests on fametrano alone. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/graphs/contributors
code_of_conduct_justification: btclib-org/.github's CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md is this repository's code of conduct, through GitHub's organization-wide default; the community-profile API reports it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
code_review_standards_justification: REVIEWING.md states what a review checks, how a finding is written and what clears a pull request; the part shared by every repository is followed by what this tree checks in particular. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/REVIEWING.md
coding_standards_enforced_justification: ruff-check, ruff-format and mypy run as pre-commit hooks, and lint.yml runs the same .pre-commit-config.yaml in CI as a required check, so the style is enforced automatically rather than by review alone. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml
coding_standards_justification: pyproject.toml selects every ruff rule (select = ["ALL"]) with a documented ignore list, and runs mypy in strict mode. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/pyproject.toml
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the public-surface, input-validation, lint-gate and 100%-coverage requirements a contribution must meet before it can land. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contributors_unassociated_justification: fametrano is the only significant contributor. One outside contributor has made one commit: IG-ABHINAV (pull request 7, a comment in deps-latest.yml, from the good first issue 4). Counted with: git rev-list --count v2026.11.14, and git log v2026.11.14 --format=%an | sort | uniq -c. pmazzocchi and giacomocaironi, the other organization owners, have made no commit here. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/graphs/contributors
copyright_per_file_justification: Every Python file opens with "Copyright (c) The btclib developers", and ruff's flake8-copyright rule (CPY001) keeps it there, e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/src/coin_addresses/__init__.py
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The hashes are fixed by the address formats: an EVM or Tron address carries a Keccak-256 hash, and a bitcoin clone's, a Cosmos Hub's or an XRP Ledger address the RIPEMD-160 of a SHA-256, so a user cannot switch to another hash without leaving the format. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/README.md
crypto_call_justification: The package's primary purpose is not cryptography, and it holds its own implementations of two primitives, as fallbacks. It calls libraries for the rest: SHA-256 from hashlib, RIPEMD-160 and Keccak-256 from hashlib's OpenSSL where it computes them right, the parsing of a secp256k1 public key from ecc, and the Base58Check, bech32, CashAddr and strkey codecs from base58-bech32. At import, _keccak.select and _hashes.select take OpenSSL's keccak-256 and ripemd160 through hashlib.new only where it answers the known digest of the empty input, and otherwise a pure-Python fallback: where hashlib refuses the name with a ValueError, and where it answers the name with another digest. _keccak.py's fallback, pure_python_keccak_256, is the project's own Keccak-f[1600] permutation and sponge, a re-implementation of the primitive, which tests/keccak_test.py checks against the Keccak team's ShortMsgKAT_256 and against OpenSSL's on drawn inputs. _ripemd160.py's is Bitcoin Core's Python RIPEMD-160, an implementation vendored into the package with its attribution rather than called from a library, which tests/ripemd160_test.py checks against its authors' vectors and against OpenSSL's. test_select_falls_back_where_the_name_is_refused and test_select_falls_back_where_the_digest_is_wrong, in both test files, cover the two fallback cases. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/tree/main/src/coin_addresses
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: coin-addresses performs no network communications, so it uses no TLS: no module under src/ imports socket, ssl, http or urllib. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/tree/main/src/coin_addresses
crypto_credential_agility_justification: coin-addresses is a library with no configuration file, credential store or password: it derives and validates the addresses of the public keys and strings a caller passes in, and keeps nothing. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/tree/main/src/coin_addresses
crypto_floss_justification: No closed-source dependency: the standard library, and ecc and base58-bech32, both MIT. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/pyproject.toml
crypto_keylength_justification: The package generates and uses no cryptographic key. A public key a caller passes is the input an address is derived from, and SHA-256, RIPEMD-160 and Keccak-256 take no key. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/tree/main/src/coin_addresses
crypto_password_storage_justification: The package stores no password and authenticates no one: it has no user, account or secret of its own.
crypto_pfs_justification: The package implements no network key-agreement protocol: it performs no network communications at all.
crypto_published_justification: Every algorithm is a published one: SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4), RIPEMD-160, Keccak-256 (the Keccak team's SHA-3 submission, without the domain bits FIPS 202 adds), and the secp256k1 key encoding of SEC 1, through ecc. The address checksums are base58-bech32's published codecs. Each coin's addresses are checked against vectors from its specification or its reference implementation, pinned in the test files by repository, path and commit. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/README.md
crypto_random_justification: The package draws no random number: nothing under src/ imports random or secrets or reads os.urandom. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/tree/main/src/coin_addresses
crypto_tls12_justification: coin-addresses performs no network communications and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/tree/main/src/coin_addresses
crypto_used_network_justification: coin-addresses does not use the network: no module under src/ imports socket, ssl, http or urllib. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/tree/main/src/coin_addresses
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: coin-addresses performs no network communications and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/tree/main/src/coin_addresses
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No SHA-1 or MD5 appears under src/: the package hashes with SHA-256 and RIPEMD-160 (_hashes.py) and Keccak-256 (_keccak.py), the hashes the address formats require. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/tree/main/src/coin_addresses
crypto_working_justification: The package uses SHA-256, RIPEMD-160 and Keccak-256, the hashes the address formats fix, and no SHA-1 or MD5: none appears under src/.
dco_justification: main requires the lint / Sign-off check, which refuses a pull request with a commit that lacks its author's Signed-off-by: trailer. Dependabot's, pre-commit.ci's and claude[bot]'s commits are exempt. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py
delivery_mitm_justification: Distribution channels use HTTPS exclusively: GitHub, and PyPI through Trusted Publishing. [osps_br_03_02]
delivery_unsigned_justification: Releases are published to PyPI and GitHub Releases and installed with pip from PyPI, all over HTTPS. No package or hash is fetched over plain HTTP. https://pypi.org/project/coin-addresses/ https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/releases
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot version updates cover uv, github-actions and docker, and Dependabot security updates are on. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml
description_good_justification: coin-addresses derives the address a coin gives a public key, and validates an address, for Ethereum and the EVM chains, Bitcoin Cash, Bitcoin SV, Bitcoin Gold, eCash, Litecoin, Dogecoin, Dash, Tron, the Cosmos Hub, the XRP Ledger, Solana and Stellar, in typed Python. https://coin-addresses.readthedocs.io/
discussion_justification: GitHub supports discussions on issues and pull requests.
documentation_achievements_justification: README.md links the OpenSSF Scorecard, Best Practices and Baseline badges on the lines the organization standard reserves for them. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/README.md
documentation_architecture_justification: No document gives the high-level design. CONTRIBUTING.md's *The public surface* states the rules the layout follows: a module per coin family, each publishing the same three functions, and imports of the standard library, ecc and base58-bech32 alone, which tests/imports_test.py holds. The private modules the coin modules share are described only in their own docstrings. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-public-surface
documentation_basics_justification: README.md says what the package does and what it does not, and gives an example for each coin family that tests/readme_test.py runs; CONTRIBUTING.md and SECURITY.md cover the rest. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/README.md
documentation_current_justification: The docs build is gated in CI as a required check (docs.yml, `-n -W`), tests/docs_test.py fails when a shipped module has no API page, and tests/readme_test.py runs every Python block of README.md, so neither the reference generated from the docstrings nor the README's examples can drift from the code. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/.github/workflows/docs.yml
documentation_interface_justification: Every public module and function carries a docstring, gated by ruff's pydocstyle rules and pydoclint, and docs/source's automodule pages render them into the API reference published at https://coin-addresses.readthedocs.io/; tests/docs_test.py fails when a shipped module is missing from them.
documentation_quick_start_justification: README.md's *What is here* is a first use: a public key's Ethereum address and its validation, then the addresses of the bitcoin clones, Tron, the Cosmos Hub, the XRP Ledger, Solana and Stellar. tests/readme_test.py runs every block, so they are the ones the suite checks. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/README.md#what-is-here
documentation_roadmap_justification: ROADMAP.md, organization-wide in btclib-org/.github, is reviewed every September and states what is maintained, what is intended and what is deliberately not. This repository's README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md link it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/ROADMAP.md
documentation_security_justification: SECURITY.md's Limitations, not vulnerabilities states the known limits: secret material is not zeroized and nothing is constant-time. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/SECURITY.md#limitations-not-vulnerabilities
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The package carries no run-time assertion: ruff's S101 refuses an assert outside tests, and rg '\bassert\b' src/coin_addresses finds the word only in _ripemd160.py's docstring, where it says the vendored upstream's assert False became a CoinAddressesValueError. pytest, the mutation runs and the ClusterFuzzLite target run Python without -O, but the assertions they check are the tests' own, not the software's. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/tree/main/src/coin_addresses
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No fuzzing or mutation-testing finding is open: no issue in the tracker reports one. The fuzz and mutation workflows are scheduled weekly, and their run lists show each result. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/actions/workflows/fuzz.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/actions/workflows/mutation.yml
dynamic_analysis_justification: Every release runs the test suite before it is published: release.yml calls test.yml, and the PyPI upload runs only if it passes, as it did for v2026.11.14 (https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/actions/runs/43524763358). The suite fails below 100% coverage, branches included. Measured with: gh api -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github.raw' repos/btclib-org/coin-addresses/contents/pyproject.toml | grep -E '^(fail_under|branch) ', which prints branch = true and fail_under = 100.0. ClusterFuzzLite fuzzing and cosmic-ray mutation testing are scheduled weekly. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: This tree ships pure Python, a memory-safe language; it produces no software written in a memory-unsafe language for a dynamic memory-safety tool to run against. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/pyproject.toml
enhancement_responses_justification: Every enhancement request filed since the repository opened on 2026-11-12, such as issues 8, 10, 11 and 12, is the maintainer's own. Nobody else has filed one, so none is unanswered. Listed with: gh issue list -R btclib-org/coin-addresses -s all -L 500 --json number,author -q '[.[] | select(.author.login != "fametrano") | .number]', which prints []. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/issues
external_dependencies_justification: pyproject.toml declares the two runtime dependencies, base58-bech32 and ecc, beyond which tests/imports_test.py lets no module import, and the test and tooling dependencies in its dependency groups, resolved and pinned in the committed uv.lock. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/pyproject.toml
floss_license_justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
floss_license_osi_justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
governance_justification: GOVERNANCE.md, organization-wide in btclib-org/.github, documents the decision model and every role a contributor, reviewer or owner holds; this tree's README.md links it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
hardened_site_justification: Not every site sends the four headers. The project page https://btclib.org/coin-addresses/ sends Content-Security-Policy (default-src 'self', frame-ancestors 'none'), Strict-Transport-Security, X-Frame-Options DENY and X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, and the repository on github.com sends all four. The download site, PyPI's project page, sends the last three and no Content-Security-Policy. The documentation site https://coin-addresses.readthedocs.io/ is served by Read the Docs over HTTPS with Strict-Transport-Security and X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, and no Content-Security-Policy or X-Frame-Options. Measured with curl -sIL on 2026-11-14.
hardening_justification: The package uses no hardening mechanism that limits the harm of a defect left in it. What it has finds defects before a release: ruff's bandit-derived S rules, strict mypy and CodeQL. Its import-time check that OpenSSL answers the known digest of Keccak-256 and RIPEMD-160 guards against a wrong provider, not against a defect of this package. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/pyproject.toml
implement_secure_design_justification: Complete mediation: every public function checks its inputs and refuses what is invalid with the package's own errors, which tests/input_validation_test.py drives. Fail-safe defaults: is_valid_address answers False for whatever assert_valid_address refuses, which the fuzz harness checks on hostile strings. Least privilege and economy of mechanism: nothing under src/ opens a socket or draws randomness, and tests/imports_test.py lets a module import only the standard library, ecc and base58-bech32. A refusal never quotes the key or address it was handed, which each coin's tests check with tests/secret_free/'s assert_secret_free. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-public-surface
input_validation_justification: Every public function validates its inputs and refuses what is invalid with a CoinAddressesTypeError or CoinAddressesValueError, as CONTRIBUTING.md's *The public surface* requires. tests/input_validation_test.py drives the rule over every public function, and fuzz/fuzz_addresses.py holds every coin's validator to it on hostile strings. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-public-surface
installation_common_justification: The package is on PyPI, so `python -m pip install coin-addresses` installs it and `pip uninstall coin-addresses` removes it. pypi-install.yml installs the published version on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows weekly and in every release run, as it did for v2026.11.14 (https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/actions/runs/43524763358). https://pypi.org/project/coin-addresses/
installation_development_quick_justifica: `uv sync` installs the whole development environment in one command, uv being the only tool to install first; CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* section gives it beside `uv run pytest` and the lint gate. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-environment-and-the-gates
installation_standard_variables_justific: Installation is `pip install`, which follows pip's and the interpreter's own install-location conventions; there is no project-specific installer that could diverge from that convention. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/pyproject.toml
interfaces_current_justification: ruff's UP and FA rules flag deprecated constructs, and pytest turns every warning into an error. deps-latest and deps-oldest are scheduled weekly, at the newest and at the floor versions. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/pyproject.toml
internationalization_justification: The package produces no text for end users and sorts none: it derives ASCII addresses from public keys and validates them, and its exceptions are English messages for developers. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/tree/main/src/coin_addresses
know_common_errors_justification: The primary developer knows the weaknesses that apply here and counters each: improper input validation (CWE-20) by the rules of CONTRIBUTING.md's *The public surface*, which tests/input_validation_test.py drives, with the fuzz harness over every validator; sensitive information in an error message (CWE-209) by the standard's section 7, *A refusal carries no secret*, which each coin's tests check with tests/secret_free/'s assert_secret_free, and which SECURITY.md makes a reportable vulnerability. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/SECURITY.md#what-belongs-here
know_secure_design_justification: The primary developer, fametrano, wrote this package's rules on inputs and refusals (CONTRIBUTING.md's *The public surface*) and most of base58-bech32's ASSURANCE_CASE.md, which applies Saltzer and Schroeder's principles one by one: 5 of its 7 commits, counted with git log --format=%an -- ASSURANCE_CASE.md | sort | uniq -c in a base58-bech32 clone. No security review of this repository has been done. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-review
license_location_justification: Non-trivial license location file in repository: <https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/LICENSE>.
license_per_file_justification: Every Python file states "Distributed under the MIT software license, see the accompanying LICENSE file or https://opensource.org/license/mit", e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/src/coin_addresses/__init__.py
maintained_justification: The repository opened on 2026-11-12. The first release, v2026.11.14, was published on 2026-11-13, after 22 pull requests merged, and pull requests have merged on main since. Counted with: gh release list -R btclib-org/coin-addresses --json tagName -q length, which prints 1, and gh pr list -R btclib-org/coin-addresses -s merged -B main -L 500 -S 'merged:<=2026-11-13T23:13:17Z' --json number -q length, which prints 22. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/releases
maintenance_or_update_justification: Only the latest release is supported and nothing is backported (SECURITY.md). release.yml compares each release's public API with the previous tag's using griffe, and RELEASE_NOTES.md lists what a user must act on to upgrade: v2026.11.14, the first release, says there is no earlier version to upgrade from. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md
no_leaked_credentials_justification: detect-secrets baseline gated by pre-commit, and GitHub secret scanning with push protection enabled on the repository: https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/.secrets.baseline
osps_ac_01_01_justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication of every member and accepts only secure methods, not SMS. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882
osps_ac_02_01_justification: A new member gets read access, the organization's base permission (gh api orgs/btclib-org --jq .default_repository_permission). Every higher grant is assigned by hand, through an issue in btclib-org/.github that an owner other than the one asking approves. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#how-a-decision-is-made
osps_ac_03_01_justification: The main-self-merge ruleset requires a pull request for every change to main. Its one bypass actor, fametrano, holds it in pull_request mode, which excuses the approval but still refuses a direct push, so nobody pushes to main directly. Every commit on main but the root came through a pull request; the rulesets were created after the root was pushed, as REPOSITORY.md says. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/REPOSITORY.md#branch-protection
osps_ac_03_02_justification: The main-integrity ruleset forbids deleting main and has no bypass actor. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets
osps_ac_04_01_justification: The default GITHUB_TOKEN is read-only at the organization and the repository, and cannot approve pull requests. Every workflow also sets permissions: contents: read at the top. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_ac_04_02_justification: Every workflow sets permissions: contents: read at the top, and a job adds a write scope only where it uses it. zizmor's excessive-permissions audit runs in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#what-every-workflow-does
osps_br_01_01_justification: No workflow uses pull_request_target or workflow_run. Event fields and inputs reach run: steps only through env:, and zizmor's template-injection audit in the required lint check refuses the unsafe form. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml
osps_br_01_03_justification: Pull-request runs use the pull_request and pull_request_review_comment triggers, which give a fork no secrets and a read-only token. The review job, which holds a secret, runs only when the head repository is this one. The mention job holds a secret on any pull request's issue comment, and there checks out the default branch. It answers only a comment whose author is an owner, a member or a collaborator, and its tools exclude Bash, edits, writes, file reads and every tool that runs code. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/workflows/reusable-claude-review.yml
osps_br_01_04_justification: A workflow_dispatch input is either mutation.yml's profile, a choice from a fixed list, or verified-signatures.yml's before and after, which the called workflow reads through env: and refuses unless they are commit shas. osps_qa_04_01_justification: The organization standard's section 2 (*Which repositories, and how far*) lists every repository of btclib-org and its tier, coin-addresses among them, and the organization profile lists the published packages. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#which-repositories-and-how-far

osps_qa_05_02_justification: No executable, library or compiled file is committed. The Sphinx inventories under docs/source/_inventories/ and the fuzz seeds under fuzz/corpus/ are data, and .clusterfuzzlite/build.sh is the only file with the executable bit, a shell script.
osps_qa_06_01_justification: Not every commit is accepted after a suite has run. test.yml runs the suite on every push to main, and on every pull request that is not a draft and changes more than prose. osps_qa_06_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives the command that runs the suite. osps_qa_06_03_justification: The policy is 100% line and branch coverage (CONTRIBUTING.md, standard section 8). pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100, so untested new code fails the required test check. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/pyproject.toml
osps_qa_07_01_justification: The main-self-merge ruleset requires one approving review from somebody other than the author before a merge to main, and dismisses an approval on a new push. Its bypass list holds one actor, fametrano, in pull_request mode: the organization-wide bypass the maintainer keeps until the backlog settles (btclib-org/.github#2021), read with gh api repos/btclib-org/coin-addresses/rulesets/27111571 --jq '.bypass_actors, .rules' on 2026-11-14. GOVERNANCE.md asks for no bypass actor in a repository whose README carries the Best Practices badge, and records the deviation. The bypass is used for ordinary work: of the 22 pull requests merged before v2026.11.14, 18 had no approval from anybody other than their author. Counted with: gh pr list -R btclib-org/coin-addresses -s merged -B main -L 500 -S 'merged:<=2026-11-13T23:13:17Z' --json author,reviews -q '[.[] | .author.login as $a | select(any(.reviews[]; .state == "APPROVED" and .author.login != $a) | not)] | length', and for the total the same with -q length. The ruleset's history holds one version, which requires that approval, read with gh api repos/btclib-org/coin-addresses/rulesets/27111571/history (with admin rights), so each of the 18 merged through the bypass; fametrano merged all 18, counted with gh pr list -R btclib-org/coin-addresses -s merged -B main -L 500 -S 'merged:<=2026-11-13T23:13:17Z' --json author,reviews,mergedBy -q '[.[] | .author.login as $a | select(any(.reviews[]; .state == "APPROVED" and .author.login != $a) | not) | .mergedBy.login] | group_by(.) | map("\(.[0]) \(length)")'. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#how-a-decision-is-made
osps_sa_01_01_justification: The documentation holds no design document demonstrating the actions and actors within the system. osps_sa_02_01_justification: The API reference at https://coin-addresses.readthedocs.io/ is generated from the docstrings of every public module, and tests/docs_test.py fails when a shipped module is missing from it. CONTRIBUTING.md's The public surface states what is public.
osps_sa_03_01_justification: No security assessment of this repository is recorded. osps_sa_03_02_justification: No threat model or attack surface analysis of this repository is written down. osps_vm_01_01_justification: SECURITY.md's *Reporting a vulnerability* gives the private channels, a GitHub security advisory or email, and the timeframes: a report is acknowledged within 7 days, and a fix or a published advisory follows within 90 days. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability
osps_vm_02_01_justification: SECURITY.md names the security contacts: a private GitHub security advisory, or email to security at btclib dot org. btclib-org/.github's GOVERNANCE.md, *Roles*, says that address reaches every organization owner. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
osps_vm_03_01_justification: Private vulnerability reporting is enabled, and SECURITY.md points to it (opening a security advisory) and gives an email address as the alternative. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/security/advisories/new
osps_vm_04_01_justification: Vulnerabilities are published as GitHub security advisories on this repository, each naming the release that fixes it. None has been published yet. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/security/advisories
osps_vm_04_02_justification: The CycloneDX SBOM a release attaches lists, in its vulnerabilities array, every vulnerability that the tree's .github/vex.toml judges not to affect the release, with the reason. osps_vm_05_01_justification: The standard sets the threshold: actions/dependency-review-action fails a pull request that adds or changes a dependency with an advisory of moderate severity or above, or with a licence outside the allow-list. osps_vm_05_02_justification: release.yml runs uv audit over the dependencies the wheel declares, base58-bech32 and ecc, and every publish job needs it to succeed, as it did for v2026.11.14 (https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/actions/runs/43524763358). The only exemption is an id that the tree's own .github/vex.toml, carried into the release's signed SBOM, states as not affecting it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#12-releasing
osps_vm_05_03_justification: The required lint check audits the whole uv.lock, every dependency group, on every pull request that is not a draft: check_audit.py --all-groups runs uv audit, which reads OSV's malicious-package (MAL-) entries as well as advisories. The required Dependency review check also blocks a change that adds a dependency with an advisory of moderate severity or above, or a licence outside the allow-list. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#12-releasing https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_vm_06_01_justification: The standard's section 5 sets a threshold of zero for ruff: select = ALL, bandit's S rules included, and each finding is fixed or suppressed in place with a reason. zizmor holds workflows to the same, in the required lint check. osps_vm_06_02_justification: The required lint check runs .pre-commit-config.yaml on every pull request that is not a draft (ruff with the S rules, strict mypy, zizmor, detect-secrets) and blocks the merge on any finding not suppressed in place with a reason. regression_tests_added50_justification: The one defect of the package's code fixed so far, issue 31 (xrp refused a released memoryview with a bare ValueError), was fixed by pull request 34, which changes tests/xrp_test.py. test_justification: test.yml runs the suite, gated at 100% line and branch coverage, against vectors from each format's specification and reference implementations, each pinned in its test file by repository, path and commit: EIP-55's test cases and go-ethereum's, the Keccak team's ShortMsgKAT_256, the RIPEMD-160 authors' vectors as Bitcoin Core carries them, the CashAddr specification, the key and address tests of Bitcoin Cash Node, Bitcoin ABC, Bitcoin SV, Bitcoin Gold, Litecoin, Dogecoin and Dash, and those of java-tron, cosmos-sdk, rippled, solana-sdk and SEP-0023. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md makes 100% coverage a gate every change must pass, so new functionality comes with its tests. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-environment-and-the-gates
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires 100% line and branch coverage, and fail_under = 100.0 fails the CI gate on any new code without a test. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_statement_coverage80_justification: pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100.0, gated by test.yml on every pull request that is not a draft and changes more than prose. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/pyproject.toml
test_statement_coverage90_justification: pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100.0 under [tool.coverage.report], and the required test check enforces it on every pull request that is not a draft and changes more than prose: https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/pyproject.toml
tests_are_added_justification: The required check test: every job passed fails a pull request that is not a draft and leaves a line or branch untested. Its coverage job runs on any such pull request that changes src/, which the prose-pattern never matches, so a change to src/ lands without its tests only through an administrator's merge, which waits for no required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents the 100% coverage gate, so new functionality without a test fails the required test check. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
two_person_review_justification: Of the 22 pull requests merged before v2026.11.14, the only release, 4 were approved by somebody other than the author, 18%, below the 50% the criterion asks; none was approved by somebody other than fametrano. Counted with: gh pr list -R btclib-org/coin-addresses -s merged -B main -L 500 -S 'merged:<=2026-11-13T23:13:17Z' --json author,reviews -q '[.[] | .author.login as $a | select(any(.reviews[]; .state == "APPROVED" and .author.login != $a))] | length'; for the total, the same with -q length; for the approvals by somebody other than fametrano, the same with .author.login != "fametrano" added to the select. main's ruleset requires one approving review from somebody other than the author, and fametrano holds a pull_request-mode bypass of it, read with gh api repos/btclib-org/coin-addresses/rulesets/27111571 --jq '.bypass_actors, .rules'. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/2021
updateable_reused_components_justificati: At run time the package reuses the standard library, and base58-bech32 and ecc, PyPI packages declared with a floor in pyproject.toml. The test and tooling components are PyPI packages pinned in uv.lock and bumped by Dependabot, and the deps-latest sentinel is scheduled to run the full suite against the upgraded set every week. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/.github/workflows/deps-latest.yml
version_semver_justification: CalVer, YYYY.M.D, declared in pyproject.toml and explained in RELEASE_NOTES.md: the number says when a release was cut and promises nothing about compatibility, so a breaking change is announced in RELEASE_NOTES.md. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md
version_tags_justification: Each release is tagged v<version> on the release commit, as RELEASING.md requires. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/tags
version_tags_signed_justification: Every release tag is signed: RELEASING.md tags with git tag -s and reads the signature back from the API once the tag is pushed. v2026.11.14's reads verified, reason valid, with gh api repos/btclib-org/coin-addresses/git/tags/77afad142a54ce8971e332117c288f05650be93e --jq .verification. The tag-integrity ruleset's required_signatures refuses a v* push that brings an unsigned commit, and does not check the tag's own signature, as REPOSITORY.md's *Tag protection* says. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/tags
version_unique_justification: Each release carries a unique calendar version, YYYY.M.D, declared once in pyproject.toml and tagged v<version>. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/releases
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No vulnerability in this code is known and none is unfixed: the advisories list is empty and no Dependabot alert has been raised. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/security/advisories
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No vulnerability in this code has been reported or published, and no Dependabot alert has been raised. Issue 23, labelled security, was GHSA-mmhr-3c5m-f64f in soupsieve, published on 2026-11-13, which only the docs group locks; pull request 25 moved the lock past it the same day. Each advisory would name the release that fixes it. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/security/advisories
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerability in this code has been reported to this repository, so there is no reporter to credit. SECURITY.md says how a report is made. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability report has been received since the repository opened on 2026-11-12. SECURITY.md promises an acknowledgement within 7 days. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/security/advisories
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md's Reporting a vulnerability gives the private channels (a GitHub security advisory, or security at btclib dot org), who can see a report, and how a CVE is requested. Private vulnerability reporting is enabled. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/SECURITY.md
warnings_fixed_justification: Warnings are not tolerated: ruff, strict mypy and pytest's filterwarnings = ["error"] fail the required checks. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/pyproject.toml
warnings_justification: mypy strict with all relevant extra checks activated, see https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/pyproject.toml
warnings_strict_justification: ruff runs with `select = ["ALL"]` (every rule family) and mypy runs with `strict = true`; both are zero-finding pre-commit hooks enforced again by the required lint workflow. https://github.com/btclib-org/coin-addresses/blob/main/pyproject.toml
